name: CPython
description: The reference implementation of the Python language.
summary: CPython's developer guide allows contributors to use generative AI for code, tests, documentation, comments and for understanding the code base. The submitter stays responsible for the content, must review AI output in detail and be able to explain the change in their own words; disclosing AI use in the PR description is appreciated but not required, and AI use alone is not grounds for closing a contribution.

evidence.quote: The person submitting an issue or PR is responsible for its content, regardless of whether AI tools were used in its creation.
Authors must review the work done by AI tooling in detail to ensure it actually makes sense before proposing it as a PR or filing it as an issue.
We expect PR authors and those filing issues to be able to explain their proposed changes in their own words.
Disclosure of the use of AI tools in the PR description is appreciated, while not required.
Always review the output before opening a pull request or issue, including proposed PR or issue titles and descriptions.

otherRules.description: Maintainers who think a contribution does not follow the guidelines may apply an AI-needs-explanation label (the item stays open and the author must reply in their own words explaining the change and how they checked it) or an AI-guidelines-not-met label (the item is closed).

quotes.quote: AI-needs-explanation: the issue or PR stays open. Reply in your own words: explain what the change does or what the issue is about, and describe how you checked that it is correct.

otherRules.description: Maintainers may close issues and PRs that are not useful or productive regardless of AI use, and may block contributors who repeatedly open unproductive issues or PRs.

quotes.quote: Maintainers may close issues and PRs that are not useful or productive, without explanation, regardless of whether AI tools were used or not.
